Report Studio and Custom Views

Administrators build small HTML/Jinja/JavaScript views over curated read-only datasets in Report Studio; once published they appear under Custom Views for every signed-in user of that ADOM.

👤 ForViewerOperatorAdministratorAdvanced user
🔑 Permissionsstudio.plugin_studio audit.view
📍 Whereany device ADOM → Plugins → Custom Views / Report Studio; Global ADOM → Global → Plugins → Report Studio (URLs /plugins/, /plugins/gallery)

What is it?#

Called Plugin Studio until 2026-10-22: that name now belongs to the Python studio (Script Library, console, data stores, connections, apps). Only the label changed — the URLs and the studio.plugin_studio key are the same.

Report Studio lets an administrator build a small page — a table, a set of KPI cards, a chart — from SATOM's cached fleet data, without changing SATOM's code. A plugin is a Jinja/HTML body with optional CSS and JavaScript, bound to one or more curated, read-only datasets. When it is published, every signed-in user finds it under Custom Views in the ADOM it was built in.

What does it do?#

  • Author a view: name, kind (view or widget), icon, datasets, optional Inputs, body, CSS and JavaScript.
  • Live preview the unsaved body in an isolated frame.
  • Start from an example — Browse examples offers dozens of ready-made views (fleet KPIs, device inventory, full server-policy table, traffic-log enabled policies, policies grouped by App ID, policies without a WAF profile, certificate coverage, pools by type, and more).
  • Lifecycle with gates: Draft → Testing → Published.
  • Inputs (filters the viewer fills in): Device, Select (fixed options), Text, Number, Date. Values reach the body as params.<name>.
  • Custom Views gallery: the published views of the current ADOM, each with its icon, kind and author.
  • Export / Import a plugin as a .satomplugin package to move it to another server without an update package.
  • Code plugins: install a signed package that adds its own pages at /x/<slug>/.

Available datasets#

Key Contents
fleet_appliances The managed devices visible to the viewer: name, kind, firmware, host, port
server_policies Cached FortiWeb server policies (key columns)
server_policies_full Cached server policies with traffic log, WAF profile, monitor mode, comment and parsed App ID
server_pools Cached back-end pools (type, protocol)
web_protection_profiles Cached WAF profiles (signature and bot-mitigation references)
certificates Certificate Manager certificates (no key material)
audit_recent The 200 most recent audit-log rows; empty for viewers without audit.view
fleet_counts Device, policy and certificate totals
scheduled_actions Scheduled actions (name, action, next run)

You only tick datasets; you never write SQL. Datasets are evaluated for the person viewing the page: they return only rows of the devices visible to that viewer in the current ADOM (devices in maintenance stay hidden unless the viewer's profile may see them).

Requirements#

  • Cached data in SATOM for the datasets you use (for example, server policies are only present for appliances SATOM has harvested).

Permissions#

Action Needs
Open Custom Views and view a published plugin Signed in
Open Report Studio, create, edit, save, preview, change status, delete studio.plugin_studio
View a draft or testing plugin's page or frame (including the editor's live preview) studio.plugin_studio
Export, import, and enable/disable/remove a code plugin studio.plugin_studio
Open a loaded code plugin's pages (/x/<slug>/) Signed in (the plugin may check more)

studio.plugin_studio is admin-only (only the seeded admin profile has it). Users without it get 403 on the Report Studio pages.

Every plugin action — viewing a page or its frame, editing, saving, changing status, checking status and deleting — works only on plugins of the ADOM you are in; a plugin of another ADOM cannot be reached by its address.

ℹ️Note

Changed in 2.11.0: plugins are reachable only within their own ADOM, datasets return only the viewer's visible devices (audit_recent needs audit.view), the frame no longer loads images from https: addresses, and draft/testing previews and the menu entries follow studio.plugin_studio instead of full administrator capability.

The Report Studio menu entry — under Plugins in every ADOM (in the Global ADOM: Global → Plugins, right below Automation; until 2026-10-23 it was under Administrator → Studio there) — is shown exactly to holders of studio.plugin_studio, the key the pages check. Custom Views is not offered in the Global ADOM.

How to use#

Create a view#

  1. Go to Plugins → Report Studio (any device ADOM) and click New view. The view is stamped with the ADOM you are in.
  2. Optional: click Browse examples and insert one.
  3. Fill in Name, Kind and Icon (a Bootstrap icon name such as bi-puzzle).
  4. Tick the Datasets (read-only) the body needs.
  5. Optional: under Inputs, click Add input and define Name, Label, Type, Default, Options (for Select, one per line as value|Label) and required.
  6. Write the Body (Jinja / HTML). Datasets are available as data.<key>.rows (and directly as <key>); inputs as params.<name>.
  7. Optional: add CSS and JavaScript. In JavaScript the data is available as window.pluginData and the inputs as window.pluginParams.
  8. Click Live preview to render the unsaved body in the Sandboxed preview frame.
  9. Click Save.

Publish it#

  1. In Lifecycle, click Promote to Testing and check the preview.
  2. Click Promote to Published. SATOM renders the saved body once more; if it has a render error, publishing is refused.
  3. The view now appears under Plugins → Custom Views for everyone in that ADOM.

To withdraw a view, click Disable in the Report Studio list (it returns to draft) or Back to Draft / Back to Testing in the editor.

Move a plugin to another server (export / import)#

  1. In the Report Studio list, click the download icon on the plugin's row. SATOM downloads <slug>-<version>.satomplugin (unsigned).
  2. On the other server, open Report Studio, choose the file under Import plugin and click Import.
  3. A signed package lands in Testing, an unsigned one in Draft. If a plugin with the same slug exists in this ADOM it is updated in place; an older version is refused unless you tick Allow downgrade.
  4. Promote it as usual. Updating a published view keeps it published only if the new body still renders; otherwise it goes back to Testing.

Install an app plugin (Plugin Studio)#

A package of kind app is a Plugin Studio app with what it needs: its data stores (the app's variables, with their rows), its HTTP connections without secrets and their API Catalog versions.

  1. Open Plugin Studio → Apps, click Import app package and choose the file; the import starts as soon as you pick it (tick Allow downgrade first to install an older version over a newer one). The Report Studio import accepts it too.
  2. SATOM creates what is missing — API versions (published), connections (without a secret), data stores (with their rows) — and the app's draft. An existing data store keeps its rows, an existing connection is never changed, and an installed app keeps its published version and access list.
  3. Set the secret of each new connection (Plugin Studio → Connections), review the variables in the data stores, test the draft and Publish.

spo-fortiweb (new FortiWeb server policy with DDI reservation, certificate, capacity-based FortiWeb choice and rollback) is installed this way.

Install a code plugin#

  1. Under Import plugin, choose a signed code plugin package and click Import.
  2. The Code plugins card lists it as restart required. Run satom execute restart-all on the server.
  3. After the restart the card shows loaded and an Open button to /x/<slug>/.
  4. Disable / Enable and Remove also take effect at the next restart.

Use a custom view#

  1. Go to Plugins → Custom Views and click a card.
  2. If the view has inputs, fill them in the bar above the frame; Reset restores the defaults.

Configuration#

Field Description Required Example
Name Display name; the address slug is derived from it once, at creation Yes Policies without a WAF profile
Kind view or widget Yes view
Icon Bootstrap icon class (max 32 characters) No bi-shield
Datasets One or more keys from the table above No server_policies_full
Inputs Viewer filters: Device, Select, Text, Number, Date No device input named dev
Body Jinja/HTML, rendered in a sandbox Yes {{ data.fleet_counts.rows[0].devices }}
CSS / JavaScript Inline style and script for the frame No —

Example#

🧪Example — Device count card

Tick fleet_counts, body: <h2>Fleet</h2><p>Devices: {{ data.fleet_counts.rows[0].devices }}</p>. Live preview shows the number; promote to Testing, then Published.

Result#

  • Saving, changing status and deleting are written to the audit log as plugin.save, plugin.status and plugin.delete; packages as plugin.import, plugin.export and plugin.code.install / .enable / .disable / .remove.
  • The Report Studio list shows, per plugin, the imported package version and whether it was signed or unsigned (authored here when it was never imported).
  • A published view is listed in Custom Views of its ADOM. Its address is /plugins/view/<slug>, and it opens only while you are in that ADOM.

Troubleshooting#

"A name is required."#

Possible causes - The Name field was empty on save.

"Move the view to “testing” and preview it before publishing."#

Possible causes - You tried to publish directly from draft.

Solution 1. Click Promote to Testing first, then Promote to Published.

"Cannot publish — the view still has a render error: …"#

Possible causes - The saved body raises an error with its default input values — an unknown variable (undefined values are errors), a typo in a dataset key, or a blocked operation.

Solution 1. Fix the body, Save, check Live preview, then publish again.

Verification - The preview shows the view instead of a red Plugin render error card.

"Import refused: …"#

Possible causes - The file is not a .satomplugin package, is larger than 10 MB, or holds a file the manifest does not list. - A file does not match its sha256 (it was changed after the package was built). - The package is signed by a key this server does not trust, or the signature does not match — such a package is refused, never imported as unsigned. - A code plugin is unsigned. Unsigned code is never installed. - The installed version is newer (tick Allow downgrade), the package needs a newer SATOM (min_satom), or the slug belongs to another ADOM's plugin.

A code plugin shows "error" in the Code plugins card#

Possible causes - A file in data/plugins/code/<slug>/ was changed or added after install (every start re-verifies the signature and each file), or the plugin raised an error while loading. The card shows the message; SATOM starts normally without that plugin.

Solution 1. Import the package again (same or newer version) and run satom execute restart-all.

A red "Plugin render error" card appears in the frame#

Possible causes - The body failed to render. The card shows the error type and message; the rest of the page keeps working.

The view is empty#

Possible causes - The dataset is empty on this installation, or its query failed (the dataset then carries an error note), or the inputs filtered everything out. - The viewer cannot see the devices the rows belong to (another ADOM, or in maintenance), or the view uses audit_recent and the viewer lacks audit.view.

"No published custom views in this ADOM yet."#

Possible causes - Views are ADOM-scoped. A view published in the FortiWeb ADOM is not listed in the FortiADC ADOM, and vice versa.

Advanced#

Advanced The sandbox
  • The body renders in Jinja's immutable sandbox with auto-escaping; attempts to call mutating methods or reach Python internals raise a security error.
  • Datasets are fixed, read-only queries (sensitive columns masked, at most 1,000 rows each). Input values never reach SQL — they only filter rows already loaded.
  • The output is served only inside an <iframe sandbox="allow-scripts"> without allow-same-origin, with a restrictive Content-Security-Policy: the plugin's JavaScript cannot read SATOM's cookies, page or session and cannot call SATOM. Images are allowed only from data: URLs, so the plugin's code cannot send data out to an external host through image requests.
Advanced Plugin packages and code plugins
  • A .satomplugin file is a zip: plugin.json (manifest and the sha256 of every file), an optional plugin.sig (Ed25519 over plugin.json) and the files it lists — body.jinja, style.css, script.js for views and widgets, code/<entry>/… (text files only) for code plugins.
  • A code plugin's __init__.py defines a Flask blueprint bp; SATOM mounts it at /x/<slug>/ behind sign-in. It runs with SATOM's own privileges, which is why only packages signed by a trusted key are installed.
  • Code plugins live in data/plugins/code/, so the HA standby receives them with the data sync and loads them at its own next restart.
Advanced What a published view exposes

A published view is offered to every signed-in user of its ADOM, but each viewer's datasets are filtered to the devices that viewer can see (ADOM and maintenance visibility), and audit_recent is empty for viewers without audit.view. Other datasets do not check the viewer's own permissions, so choose datasets for a published view with its whole audience in mind.
